speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: The majority of the amendments fall within the following five groups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: First, amendments to update the service provisions under various legislation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Second, amendments arising from the repeal of the Private Hospitals and Medical Clinics Act 1980.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Third, amendment of provisions to provide for the payment of financial penalties into the Consolidated Fund.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Fourth, amendments to common terms used in various legislation for alignment and consistency.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: The rest of the amendments make changes to individual Acts, which I will also take Members through.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: These amendments relate to the manner in which service of documents may be effected on a person and updates it in view of technology such as email, which is widely used today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: This allows for a greater flexibility in effecting such service.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Clauses 3, 4, 10, 11, 16, 18, 22, 24 and 28 amend various legislation, namely, the CareShield Life and Long-Term Care Act 2019 (or CSHL), the Criminal Procedure Code 2010, the Human Biomedical Research Act 2015, the Human Organ Transplant Act 1987, the Medical and Elderly Care Endowment Schemes Act 2000, the National Registry of Diseases Act 2007, the Personal Data Protection Act 2012, the Termination of Pregnancy Act 1974, and the Voluntary Sterilisation Act 1974.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: These are to update the definitions or remove obsolete references as a consequence of the repeal of the Private Hospitals and Medical Clinics Act 1980 (or PHMCA) and the enactment of the Healthcare Services Act 2020 (or HCSA) which replaces it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Clause 13 amends section 41D of the Interpretation Act 1965 to align with the amendments made by the Family Justice Reform Act 2023 and the expressions used in the Family Justice Rules 2024 and Family Justice (Probate and Other Matters) Rules 2024.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: The amendment provides for the retention of old expressions for proceedings commenced before 15 October 2024 in the Family Justice Courts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Clause 13 also replaces references to commencement dates in sections 41A, 41D and 41E of the Interpretation Act 1965 with actual dates for clarity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Clause 14 updates section 4(1) of the Legitimacy Act 1934 to replace the reference to "originating summons" with "an originating application" so that the procedure for making an application under section 4(1) is consistent with the procedure adopted in probate proceedings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Clause 29 repeals superseded amendments in 11 Acts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: This aligns with similar requirements for advances from the Contingencies Fund for the Consolidated Fund and formalises what MOF is already doing in practice today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Moving on, clause 7 amends section 26 of the Employment Act 1968 (or EA) to align the EA with existing provisions under the MediShield Life Scheme Act 2015 (or MSHL) and the CSHL, which permits the deductions by employers of defaulters under the respective sections of the MSHL and CSHL to facilitate premium recovery.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Next, clause 9 makes two amendments to the Housing and Development Act 1959.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: It empowers HDB to make rules allowing the Minister for National Development to designate a Second Minister for his or her Ministry to hear and determine appeals and it deletes section 50(11) which is now obsolete as the policy regarding purchase of flats by owners of commercial property has been operationalised through the Housing and Development (Exemptions from Section 50(1) of Act) Notification 2023.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Clause 12(1) deletes an uncommenced provision in the Immigration (Amendment) Act 2023 relating to visa requirements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Clause 12(2) makes a technical amendment to section 9B of the Immigration Act 1959 to replace "territory" with "country" for consistency with the terminology used in the rest of the Immigration Act 1959.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Clause 17 amends the Medical Registration Act 1997 as follows.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Clause 17 amends section 10 of the Medical Registration Act 1997 to provide for the appointment of an executive director to the Singapore Medical Council (SMC), in addition to the executive secretary and other employees which are presently provided for.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Clause 17 updates the name of Duke-NUS Graduate Medical School Singapore to Duke-NUS Medical School Singapore in section 25(3) of the Medical Registration Act 1997, reflecting the official name change that occurred in 2015.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Clause 25 amends section 29(7) of the Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) Act 1993 by providing that forfeited items may be delivered to an authorised officer appointed under section 19 of that Act.
